chunks: Among the conditions of the religion of the Imamiyya are: certainty, sincerity, reliance on God, contentedness, submission, piety, striving, asceticism, worship, honesty, earnestness, returning trusts to the righteous and the transgressors — even to the killer of al-Husayn (peace be upon him); goodness to parents, chivalry, patience, bravery, avoiding the forbidden, cutting off covetousness of what is in the hands of people, enjoining good and forbidding evil, jihad in the way of Allah with one's self and wealth according to its conditions

giving comfort to brothers, recompensing for acts of kindness, thanking the bestower of blessings, praising the doer of good, contentment, maintaining family ties, goodness to fathers and mothers, being a good neighbor, fairness, altruism, accompanying the virtuous, keeping away from the wicked, dealing with people with beauty, greeting all people along with the conviction that the peace of Allah does not reach the oppressors, honoring the gray-haired Muslim, revering the elder, showing mercy to the young, honoring the noble of every community, humility, submissiveness, abundant remembrance of Allah (Mighty and Majestic), recitation of the Quran, supplication, lowering the gaze, forbearance, good social conduct, taqiyya, good companionship, suppressing anger, compassion toward the poor and needy and sharing with them in livelihood, fearing Allah in private and in public, goodness to women and those whom the right hand possesses, guarding the tongue except in good, having a good opinion of Allah (Mighty and Majestic), remorse over sin, practicing generosity and magnanimity, acknowledging one's shortcomings, practicing all noble deeds and moral virtues in religious and worldly matters, avoiding their blameworthy counterparts in summary and in detail

avoiding anger, displeasure, fanatical zeal, tribalism, arrogance, coercion, contempt of people, pride, self-conceit, obscenity, indecency, transgression, severing family ties, envy, greed, gluttony, covetousness, roughness, ignorance, foolishness, lying, treachery, sinfulness, debauchery, false oaths, concealing testimony, bearing false witness, backbiting, slander, tale-bearing, verbal abuse, cursing, defamation, plotting, deception, treachery, breaking covenants, killing without right, oppression, hardheartedness, harshness, hypocrisy, ostentation, adultery, sodomy, usury, fleeing from battle, reverting to desert ways after emigration, disobeying parents, deceiving people, consuming the wealth of orphans unjustly, and falsely accusing chaste women.

key_terms.التَّقِيَّة: Taqiyya — religiously sanctioned dissimulation to protect oneself or others from harm
key_terms.الْأَمْر بِالْمَعْرُوف وَالنَّهْي عَنِ ا: Enjoining good and forbidding evil — a communal religious duty
key_terms.الْإِمَامِيَّة: The Imamiyya — the Shia community that recognizes the Imams as divinely appointed successors
key_terms.الْمُرُوءَة: Chivalry, manliness — the code of noble conduct
key_terms.الْوَرَع: Piety, scrupulousness — avoiding anything doubtful out of reverence for God
key_terms.شَرَائِط: Conditions, prerequisites — the essential requirements of belonging to the religion
key_terms.صِلَة الرَّحِم: Maintaining family ties — a major ethical obligation in Islamic tradition

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions and requirements of the Imamiyya religion according to Sheikh al-Saduq?
ai.summary: This hadith from Sheikh al-Saduq's Amali (Assembly 93, 368 AH) presents a comprehensive ethical manifesto of the Imamiyya faith, enumerating over sixty positive qualities required of believers and an equal number of forbidden vices. Addressed to the Shia community of 4th-century Khorasan, this text reflects the community's need to define its religious identity through both inner spiritual qualities (certainty, sincerity, taqwa) and outward social conduct (fairness, honoring elders, neighborliness). The remarkable injunction to return trusts even to the killer of Imam Husayn (as) captures the Imamiyya's commitment to absolute honesty as a religious duty transcending personal and communal grievance.
